protocol: START Triage (Simple Triage And Rapid Treatment)
purpose: Rapidly sort multiple casualties into treatment priority categories using ability to walk, breathing, perfusion, and mental status.
steps: Step 1 - Ambulatory check: If the patient can walk, tag them MINOR and direct them to a holding/treatment area.

Step 2 - Spontaneous breathing check: If not breathing, open the airway (head-tilt/chin-lift or jaw-thrust). If still not breathing after airway is opened, tag EXPECTANT (deceased/not expected to survive).
Step 3 - Respiratory rate check: If breathing resumes after airway positioning, or respiratory rate is greater than 30/min, tag IMMEDIATE.

Step 4 - Perfusion check: If respiratory rate is 30/min or less, check capillary refill (or radial pulse). Capillary refill greater than 2 seconds, or absent radial pulse, tags IMMEDIATE; control major bleeding.
Step 5 - Mental status check: If perfusion is normal, assess whether the patient can follow simple commands. Cannot follow commands = IMMEDIATE. Can follow commands = DELAYED.

categories.immediate: Victim has severe, life-threatening injuries requiring immediate treatment.
categories.delayed: Victim has potentially severe injuries, but treatment can be delayed up to a few hours.
categories.minor: Victim has minor injuries not requiring immediate treatment (the 'walking wounded').
categories.expectant: Victim is deceased or is not expected to survive given the severity of injury and available resources.
